coverage.remaining: None. The whole document was read.
coverage.note: 51 numbered-address mentions across 53 pages, on 50 distinct addresses, recorded as 53 findings — 624 Taylor Street, 609 Sutter Street and 400 Post Street each carry two dated events. The document is unusually address-dense for a citywide theme: it names a building, a year, an architect and the organisation it was built for in the same clause, over and over. Two things shape the reading. Nearly every address is inside a parenthesis in running prose or in a figure caption, so a grep for a capitalised street name misses the numbered streets and avenues — 2700 45th Avenue, 3543 18th Street, 2850 19th Avenue — and the document has to be read rather than searched. And its footnotes are numbered and rendered inline by pdftotext, so every number was checked against the character before it; none of the 51 turned out to be a footnote marker. Appendices: none. The evaluation criteria section, half the document, is a framework rather than a record, and its only addresses are the worked examples in the figure captions, which are counted above.

findings.description: Rebuilt after the 1906 earthquake for the Chee Kung Tong, the Chinese Free Masons, founded in 1848 and headquartered here for all its societies in the United States. A purpose-built Masonic temple for the tong stood on this street as early as the 1880s. Masonic emblems survive at street level and on the second floor, and a square and compass is set into the facade.
